staticEvidence.finding: GET /ready pings Redis and returns 503 when redis is disconnected.
Redis client uses ioredis with lazyConnect, short timeouts and bounded retries.
Distributed rate limit is backed by Redis.
Compose declares a redis service and injects REDIS_URL.
Redis is documented as integrated with readiness.

hypotheses.summary: Distributed rate limit depends on Redis.
Redis client is singleton with bounded retries and timeouts.
There is a memory fallback for Redis.
Redis is an operational runtime component.
Master Catalog has direct Redis dependency.
Auth has direct Redis dependency in the inspected path.
Test bootstrap changes Redis runtime policy.
Readiness failure without Redis is expected.

riskRegister.risk: Readiness may block Go/No-Go even when API and database are healthy if Redis is absent.
Distributed rate limiting loses backend availability when Redis is unavailable.
Staging or VPS validation can fail without a Redis service or injected Redis URL.

gaps: No evidence of a sanctioned fallback for Redis absent environments.
No code change was made to soften readiness semantics.
No secondary auth path using Redis was validated in this audit.
goNoGoImpacts: Release readiness requires Redis availability where /ready is enforced.
Staging smoke checklist already treats Redis as a prerequisite.
Rate limit protection remains coupled to Redis availability.
